questions.question: 1. Which of the following is NOT an example of a descriptive analytics tool used in HR?
options: Mean and standard deviation
Counts and ratios
Decision trees and random forests
Mode and median
questions.explanation: Decision trees and random forests are predictive analytics / machine learning tools, whereas mean, median, standard deviation, counts, and ratios are descriptive analytics tools.

questions.question: 2. HR analytics differs from HRMIS primarily because HR analytics has the potential to connect HR processes and decisions with ______.
options: Employee satisfaction scores only
Regulatory compliance requirements
Payroll and compensation structures
Organization performance
questions.explanation: HR analytics connects HR processes and strategic decisions directly with organizational performance and business outcomes, moving beyond operational record-keeping typical of HRMIS.

questions.question: 3. According to the criteria for good HR activity metrics, every metric must explicitly describe what it does NOT include. This rule primarily ensures ______.
options: That metrics are visually appealing in dashboards
Clarity and prevention of misinterpretation of calculations
That metrics are aligned with competitor benchmarks
That only positive outcomes are measured and reported
questions.correctAnswer: Clarity and prevention of misinterpretation of calculations
questions.explanation: Explicitly stating exclusions ensures clarity, consistent definitions, and prevents misinterpretation or manipulation in metric calculation.

questions.question: 4. According to the criteria for good HR activity metrics, an organization should capture and track all possible metrics, even those not currently being used, to build a comprehensive data history.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Tracking unnecessary metrics leads to metric clutter, wasted resources, and analysis paralysis. Effective metrics focus specifically on actionable, strategically aligned needs.

questions.question: 5. A good HR problem definition must cover three elements. Which of the following correctly lists all three?
options: A statement of what, a statement of why, and a desired state or outcome
A statement of who, a statement of when, and a budget estimate
A statement of the problem, a timeline, and a team assignment
A cost-benefit analysis, a risk assessment, and an expected output
questions.correctAnswer: A statement of what, a statement of why, and a desired state or outcome
questions.explanation: A complete problem definition requires articulating what the issue is, why it matters, and the target/desired outcome.

questions.question: 6. The overconfidence trap is described as particularly dangerous because it prevents analysts and decision makers from ______.
options: Using advanced statistical tools
Questioning their methods, motivation, and the way they communicate findings
Collaborating with HR business partners
Collecting sufficient sample data for analysis
questions.correctAnswer: Questioning their methods, motivation, and the way they communicate findings
questions.explanation: The overconfidence trap makes analysts overly certain about conclusions, preventing critical questioning of assumptions, methods, and communication.

questions.question: 7. Which of the following best describes the 'overfitting trap' in HR analytics?
options: The analyst uses too few variables to build a reliable model
The analyst collects more data than is needed for the analysis
The visualization uses too many chart types, causing confusion
The model performs well on training data but poorly on new real-world data
questions.correctAnswer: The model performs well on training data but poorly on new real-world data
questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a statistical or machine learning model fits noise and specific artifacts of historical training data, failing on new real-world data.

questions.question: 8. In the stakeholder engagement framework for HR analytics, data owners, technology owners, and subject matter experts are classified as ______.
options: Stakeholders served
Stakeholders depended upon
Stakeholders impacted
Stakeholders managed
questions.explanation: Analysts depend upon data owners, IT/technology owners, and SMEs to acquire data access, infrastructure, and contextual validation.

questions.question: 9. Which of the following correctly lists the four components of the 'Six Skills for Success' category called 'Business Acumen'?
options: Data awareness, Statistical methods, Visualization, Writing
Problem definition, Project management, Change management, Stakeholder management
Financial literacy, Political astuteness, Internal awareness, External awareness
HR sub-functions, HR interdependencies, Privacy, Ethics
questions.correctAnswer: Financial literacy, Political astuteness, Internal awareness, External awareness
questions.explanation: The Business Acumen competency includes Financial literacy, Political astuteness, Internal organizational awareness, and External market awareness.

questions.question: 10. Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between KPIs and HR metrics?
options: KPIs and HR metrics are completely unrelated measurement tools
HR metrics are a broader category, and every KPI is a metric
KPIs replace traditional HR metrics in modern organizations
HR metrics only apply to recruitment; KPIs apply to all functions
questions.correctAnswer: HR metrics are a broader category, and every KPI is a metric
questions.explanation: Metrics represent the broader umbrella of all measurable values; KPIs are a strategic subset of metrics focused on critical goals.
